These two analyses demonstrated the benefits of this project from both a holistic sustainability perspective as well as an economic perspective. Multiple impact categories in the LCA were investigated including global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, marine and freshwater eutrophication, as well as water deprivation. These impacts were calculated using ReCiPe 2016, Cumulative Energy Demand, and AWARE water footprint calculation methods. All these impact categories as well as the capital expenditure (CAPEX) and OPEX costs of the TEA were levelized per m3 of treated water to provide a standard basis between Applications. A summary table describing the impact in each category normalized per m3 of product water (mainstream water treated) can be seen in Table ES-3. The baseline and final scenario can be seen for each Application (with an intermediate step for the MagPrex® initial implementation), along with the associated percent improvement that resulted from the optimization work related to this project.
